brief: a study script (`study.py`) that explores the discovery half of 8 real FiveThirtyEight surveys (codebook under Task inputs; data/<dataset>.csv) and prints one JSON claim {dataset, x, x_level, y, y_level, direction}. The host re-tests the claim on a hidden replication half (Spearman, p < 0.01, same sign) and scores the codebook wording of x and y with a frozen judge trained on real Ig Nobel winners vs ordinary paper titles; loss = 1 - min(1, |rho_rep|/0.2) * ignobel_likeness (0 if it fails to replicate or is trivial: same question, near-identical wording, or two demographics). The record to beat is a brute-force discovery-half scan (macaroni and cheese goes with cheesecake), loss 0.3721
proxy_note: real FiveThirtyEight surveys; frozen text-classifier judge, not the Ig Nobel committee
